function.name: get_current_time
function.description: Get the current date, time, day of the week and timezone: the base for any date or time you compute.

function.name: request_user_selection
function.description: Ask the user to pick one or more options from a list; their pick comes back to you as the answer.

options.description: 2-6 distinct choices, each {"label": "shown to the user", "value": "returned to you"}.

multiple.description: True when the user may pick several.

context.description: Optional one line on why the choice is needed.

function.name: get_weather
function.description: The weather now and today at the user's Home zone (condition, temperature, high / low, rain chance). Use this for any "what's the weather" — not web search.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web (DuckDuckGo) for public, general information: business hours, addresses, news, product specs. Never for the user's own data (memories, calendar, calls, contacts have their own tools).

function.name: run_code
function.description: Run Python 3 in a sandbox and get back what it prints. For calculations, parsing or reshaping data, many similar tool calls in a loop, and edge cases no tool covers. Prefer a dedicated tool when one fits. The script calls your tools as `tools.NAME(arg=...)` (or `call("NAME", arg=...)`); each returns the tool's text. Reads and changes Dana can undo are allowed; tools that ask first or act outside Dana (sending, paying, deleting) raise ToolError: call those yourself. `/work` is your scratch folder, kept a day. Standard library only, no network, no input().

code.description: The Python code; print() what you need back.

function.name: add_task
function.description: Add a task to the user's task list; a time, place, car or wake-up trigger makes it a reminder.

title.description: What to do, e.g. 'Buy a gift for Maya'.

group.description: The task group by name, e.g. 'Work'; picked automatically when left out.

location.description: One of the user's zones, e.g. 'home' (get_zones maps 'work' or 'my parents' to one).

time_trigger.description: When to remind, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' (compute it with get_current_time); a time already past moves to the next day.

wake_trigger.description: True to remind when the user wakes up.

call_id.description: The phone call it came from (from list_recent_calls / search_calls); the task is linked to it.

function.name: update_task
function.description: Change a task: complete or reopen it, rename it, or change its details, group or triggers. Only what you pass changes; '' removes a field.

item.description: The task's ID (from list_tasks) or its title.

location.description: A zone to remind at (see get_zones); '' removes the location trigger.

time_trigger.description: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' (compute it with get_current_time); '' removes it.

wake_trigger.description: True to remind on waking, False to stop.

description.description: The new details (replaces them); '' clears them.

group.description: Move it to this task group by name; '' moves it to General.

function.name: delete_task
function.description: Delete a task for good (the user is asked first). A finished task is completed with update_task instead.

item.description: The task's ID (from list_tasks) or its title.

function.name: get_zones
function.description: List the user's zones: the places a location reminder can name (Home and the others they added). Call this before add_task or update_task with a location, to map what the user said ('work', 'my parents') to one of these names. If none matches, show them the list and ask; new zones are added in Settings → Zones.

function.name: list_tasks
function.description: List open tasks (or completed ones, latest first) with their IDs, groups, due dates and triggers. Not needed before update_task / delete_task when you know the title.

completed.description: True for completed tasks instead of open ones.

group.description: Only this task group, by name (e.g. 'Work').

function.name: list_task_groups
function.description: List the task groups the user can see (their own and shared ones) with emoji and task count.

function.name: add_task_group
function.description: Add a new task group for organizing tasks.

name.description: The display name for the group (e.g. 'Fitness', 'Finance').

emoji.description: An emoji icon for the group (e.g. '💪', '💰').

color.description: A hex color for the group (e.g. '#ff6b6b').

description.description: Optional description of what this group is for.

function.name: remove_task_group
function.description: Remove a task group (the user is asked first). Its tasks move to 'General'.

name.description: The name of the group to remove (e.g. 'Fitness').

function.name: get_shopping_list
function.description: Show the shopping list (groceries and supermarket products) by aisle: each item with its id, quantity and note, and what was bought. Use it to answer questions about the list; to add, tick or remove items there is no need to read it first.

function.name: add_shopping_items
function.description: Add groceries and supermarket products to the shopping list, each with its own quantity and note when the user gave them. A product already on the list is not added twice (a quantity or note given now replaces the old one); one bought before comes back to buy.

name.description: The product as the user said it, without the amount (e.g. 'חלב', 'tomatoes').

quantity.description: How much, when said: '2', '1 kg', '3 ליטר'.

note.description: A detail, when said: '3%', 'lactose-free', 'the big one'.

function.name: update_shopping_items
function.description: Mark shopping-list items bought or back to buy, remove them, or clear every bought item. Name the items as the user did, or by id; no need to read the list first.

action.description: 'bought' (ticked off), 'to_buy' (back on the list), 'remove' (delete), or 'clear_bought' (remove every bought item; no items needed).

items.description: The items, by name or id, e.g. ["milk", "bread"].

function.name: edit_shopping_item
function.description: Change one shopping-list item: its name, quantity, note or aisle. Leave out what stays; an empty text clears a quantity or note.

item.description: The item, by name or id.

quantity.description: The new quantity ('2', '1 kg'); '' clears it.

aisle.description: One of produce, bakery, dairy, meat, pantry, snacks, drinks, frozen, household, care, baby, pets, other (remembered for this name on this list).

function.name: create_project
function.description: Create a new project/topic that groups related sections, entries and tasks (e.g. wedding, trip, flat hunt). Call this only after `list_projects` shows no matching active project, and only when the topic clearly will collect multiple notes/links/tasks. The project title is a short label in the user's language; description is one sentence. The returned ID is passed to `create_section` / `save_knowledge_item`.

title.description: The name of the project (e.g. "Paris Trip 2026").

description.description: Optional one-line details about the project.

icon.description: Optional emoji icon for the project (e.g. "💍" for a wedding).

color.description: Optional accent color as a hex value (e.g. "#e11d48").

tags.description: Optional list of short labels for the project.

target_date.description: Optional ISO date the project points at (the wedding day, the flight), shown as a countdown.

budget.description: Optional total budget in the user's currency; chosen options' prices are counted against it.

function.name: list_projects
function.description: List all projects/topics (titles + IDs + entry/task counts), optionally filtered by status. Use as the first step before saving anything, to find the project to save into.

status.description: Status to filter by ('active' or 'archived'). Defaults to None (all projects).

function.name: list_project_entries
function.description: Show a project's structure: its sections (with their columns and summary state) and every entry in each (id, title, decision, column values, file count, short preview). Use this to see what a project already contains BEFORE saving anything, so you never create a duplicate of something that is already there, and to find the section to save into. Bodies are truncated — call `get_knowledge_item` with the entry ID to read one in full (with its files).

project_id.description: The ID of the project to list (from `list_projects`).

kind.description: Optional filter by kind ('note', 'record' or 'link'). Defaults to None (all kinds).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return. Defaults to 80.

function.name: get_knowledge_item
function.description: Read one saved entry in full: its Markdown body, fields, summary, tags, comments and the text of its files (a PDF's or a photo's text, a recording's transcript; read now if not yet). `search_knowledge` and `list_project_entries` only return a short preview. Use this whenever you need the actual details of a specific item (prices, contacts, decisions, dates).

item_id.description: The entry ID, as returned by `search_knowledge` or `list_project_entries`.

function.name: save_knowledge_item
function.description: Save an entry (note, record or link) into a project and return its ID (for update_knowledge_item / delete_knowledge_item / save_whatsapp_file). Check `list_project_entries` first so you never duplicate one. In an 'options' section the entry is one option: name its `fields` exactly as the section's columns, in their types.

kind.description: 'note' (free text), 'record' (structured: a vendor, a contract; give fields) or 'link' (a URL, auto-processed into a transcript, summary and media).

title.description: Short label (max ~8 words, no markdown) in the user's language, e.g. "Photographer — Yanai".

body.description: The full details as clean Markdown ('##' headings, **bold** key figures, '-' bullets); keep the user's facts, numbers, dates and wording verbatim.

fields.description: Optional facts to compare or query later: [{"name": "Price", "type": "money", "value": 4500}];

tags.description: Optional 2-4 short labels in the user's language (e.g. ["צלם", "תקציב"]).

due_at.description: Optional ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) when a deadline matters.

url.description: Optional URL to attach and auto-process (usually with kind 'link').

section.description: Optional section (title or ID) of the project to put the entry in.

decision.description: For an option: '' (just an option), 'shortlist', 'chosen' or 'rejected'.

function.name: search_knowledge
function.description: Search the knowledge base (titles, bodies, AI summaries, transcripts, tags, fields, the text of attached files) by word prefix; shows the text around each hit. Use to answer the user's questions like 'what did I save/find about X?'. Prefer 1-2 concrete keywords (in the language the content is in) over full sentences. Pass project_id to scope the search to a project.

query.description: The search term(s), e.g. "צלם" or "insurance policy".

project_id.description: Optional project ID to restrict the search to a specific project.

function.name: update_project
function.description: Update a project's metadata (partial update: only provided arguments change). Entries and tasks are not touched here — use update_knowledge_item for entries. Rename the topic, change its icon/ color/tags, or archive the whole project with status='archived' when it is finished.

project_id.description: The ID of the project to update.

target_date.description: Optional ISO date the project points at (e.g. the wedding day), or "" to clear.

budget.description: Optional total budget in the user's currency.

function.name: delete_project
function.description: Delete a project and its associated entries and tasks.

project_id.description: The ID of the project to delete.

function.name: update_knowledge_item
function.description: Edit an existing entry; only the arguments you pass change. Send only what changes: the fields that change (not the whole list) and `body_edits` for a few lines (not the whole body). Record a decision on an option with decision='chosen' / 'shortlist' / 'rejected' ('' resets); move it along with status 'in_progress' / 'done', or 'archived' to sweep it away; move it to another project with `project`.

item_id.description: The ID of the entry to update.

body.description: Optional whole new Markdown body (to rewrite it; prefer body_edits for changes).

body_edits.description: Optional exact replacements in the body, applied in order: - ..."} appends at the end.

fields.description: Optional fields to set, matched by name (others are kept):

tags.description: Optional new list of labels (replaces them).

due_at.description: Optional new ISO date, or "" to clear.

url.description: Optional new URL, or "" to clear.

section.description: Optional section (title or ID) to move the entry to, or "" for none.

project.description: Optional project (ID or title) to move the entry to; its section is cleared unless `section` names one of the new project's.

function.name: delete_knowledge_item
function.description: Delete a specific knowledge entry.

item_id.description: The ID of the entry to delete.

function.name: update_entry_file
function.description: Rename a file kept on an entry, change its note, or remove it (remove=true).

file.description: The file's ID or name, as `get_knowledge_item` lists it.

remove.description: Remove the file from the entry.

function.name: create_section
function.description: Add a section to a project. Use kind='options' for a decision among alternatives (photographers, venues, flats, flights): the options are entries in it that share the section's `columns`, and the user compares them side by side and marks one chosen. Use kind='notes' for free items (ideas, links, reminders). Check `list_project_entries` first so you never duplicate a section.

title.description: Short name in the user's language (e.g. "צלמים", "Venues").

columns.description: For 'options': the facts every option is compared on, as

summary.description: Optional Markdown write-up of the section (the TL;DR / recommendation).

function.name: update_section
function.description: Change a section (partial update). Use `summary` to write or refresh the section's Markdown write-up — for an options section: a short TL;DR comparison table, the recommendation, and what is still open — after options are added or change. `columns` are merged into the existing ones by `key` (else name): a given column changes that one (pass its `key` to rename it, keeping its values), a new one is added, {"name": ..., "remove": true} drops one; others stay.

columns.description: Optional columns to change, add or remove (see `create_section`).

summary.description: Optional new Markdown summary ("" clears it).

function.name: delete_section
function.description: Delete a section. Its entries stay in the project without a section, unless with_entries is true.

with_entries.description: Also delete the entries (and their files) in it.

function.name: remember_info
function.description: Save a durable fact about the owner in "About you" (kept at once, with an Undo button). Call it without being asked for what will still be true and useful in a month (who a person is to the owner, what a nickname, place or device name means, a standing preference or routine), and when told "remember ...". Never save passwords, codes, account or card numbers, health or money details, plans, one-time events or unconfirmed guesses. Don't re-save what your instructions already list; reply briefly ("Noted.") after saving.

fact.description: One short plain sentence in the owner's language, e.g. "Dan is Maya's brother" or "'The gate' means the front gate". Required.

section.description: people, home, habits or other. Guessed when omitted.

replaces.description: When this corrects or sharpens a fact you already have, that fact's id or text; it is rewritten instead of adding a second one.

function.name: recall_info
function.description: Search what you know about the owner ("About you" facts, plus a few older saved notes). Everything in About you is already in your instructions, so call this only to look for something specific that is not there, or to get a fact's id.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. a name ("Dan", "אמא") or a topic ("gate", "wifi").

function.name: forget_info
function.description: Remove a fact from "About you" when the owner asks you to forget it or says it is wrong. It is removed at once (Undo is offered) and will not be learned again.

fact.description: The fact's id (from recall_info / list_memories) or its text. Required.

function.name: list_memories
function.description: List the facts in "About you", optionally one section. They are already in your instructions; use this when the owner asks what you know about them, or to get ids.

section.description: people, home, habits or other. All sections when omitted.

function.name: list_people
function.description: List the people the user talks to (built from calls and messages), e.g. who he talked to lately or who he hasn't talked to in a while.

query.description: Optional name, relation or phone number to filter by (in any language or script).

sort.description: 'recent' (last contact first), 'drifting' (only people he talks to regularly but not lately), 'pinned' or 'name'.

limit.description: Max people to return (default 15, at most 50).

function.name: get_person
function.description: Everything Dana knows about one person: relation, notes, birthday, how often they talk, the AI brief (what's going on, open loops), recent calls with summaries, recent messages from them and open tasks involving them.

person.description: The person's name (in any language or script, partial is fine), phone number or id.

function.name: update_person
function.description: Update what Dana knows about a person; only what you pass changes. Creates them when nobody matches (unless rename_to is given).

person.description: The person's name, phone number or id.

relation.description: Who they are to the user, e.g. 'mother', 'colleague at Wix', 'plumber'.

notes.description: Replace the free-text notes ('' clears them).

append_note.description: Add a line to the notes (keeps what's there).

birthday.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or MM-DD when the year is unknown.

add_alias.description: Another name they go by (e.g. their name in another script, a nickname).

pinned.description: Pin (true) or unpin (false) them in the People list and the home-screen widget.

rename_to.description: A new display name (the old one stays as an alias).

function.name: link_task_to_person
function.description: Attach a task to a person so it shows on their page and on the card when they call.

task_id.description: The task's ID (from list_tasks) or its title.

person.description: The person's name, phone number or id.

function.name: list_recent_calls
function.description: The user's most recent call recordings and voice memos, newest first: id, time, who, length, title, labels and summary.

label.description: Only calls with this label: family, partner, friends, work, wedding, home, purchases, travel, car, health, pets, admin, security, tech_help, logistics, automated.

function.name: search_calls
function.description: Search the user's call recordings and voice memos by person, topic or both (names, transcripts, summaries, titles); best matches first, at most 30.

query.description: Words that must all match, in any field: a name ("אמא"), a topic ("דגים"), or both ("אמא דגים").

function.name: get_call_transcript
function.description: One call or voice memo in full: details, summary, key facts, pending suggestions, tasks from it and the transcript (a long one comes in pages).

call_id.description: The call's id, from list_recent_calls or search_calls.

offset.description: Where in the transcript to start (a long transcript's result names the next offset).

function.name: list_call_suggestions
function.description: Tasks, calendar events and security alerts suggested from the user's calls and phone notifications (newest 50), each with its id and source; nothing is created until one is accepted.

function.name: accept_call_suggestion
function.description: Create the task (or calendar event) a call or notification suggestion describes, optionally with changes. The task is linked to its source. Only call this when the user asked to create/accept it or approved your proposed version. Pass only the fields that change; everything else comes from the suggestion.

suggestion_id.description: The suggestion ID (from list_call_suggestions or the chat context).

time_trigger.description: Reminder time 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' (tasks). Compute absolute times with get_current_time.

location.description: One of the user's zones for a location trigger (call get_zones first if unsure).

wake_trigger.description: True to remind when the user wakes up.

clear_triggers.description: True to drop the suggested triggers before applying the ones given here.

function.name: dismiss_call_suggestion
function.description: Dismiss a call or notification suggestion the user doesn't want.

function.name: search_notifications
function.description: Full-text search over the notifications the user's phone received (last 30 days), e.g. a bank message, a courier update or what someone wrote.

function.name: list_notifications
function.description: List recent phone notifications with Dana's triage (priority, category, whether they need the user).

bucket.description: 'needs_you' (important or with something to do), 'normal', or 'dismiss' (suggested to dismiss). Empty = all.

app.description: Only this app (app name or Android package, e.g. 'WhatsApp').

function.name: summarize_notifications
function.description: Summarize what is waiting in the user's phone notifications Inbox: a short briefing plus one summary per app (who wrote what, what needs the user). Use for "what did I miss?" or "anything important on my phone?".

function.name: dismiss_notifications
function.description: Dismiss notifications in Dana's Inbox (they are also cleared from the phone's notification shade on its next sync). Pass either specific IDs or a bucket. Dismissed notifications can be restored from the app.

bucket.description: Dismiss every active notification in this bucket instead, usually 'dismiss' (suggested to dismiss).

function.name: snooze_notifications
function.description: Snooze notifications: hide them from Dana's Inbox and the phone's notification shade until a time, then they come back. Give either minutes or until.

until.description: Snooze until this local time, ISO format (e.g. '2026-11-10T20:00').

function.name: get_ha_exposed_entities
function.description: Live state of the Home Assistant entities exposed to the voice assistant (state, key attributes, aliases), grouped by domain. Use it for a device's current state (is it on, the temperature, what is playing) or a device missing from the Home Devices list; never just to look up ids that list already has, and never guess ids.

search.description: Only entities whose id, name, alias or domain contains this, e.g. "light", "kitchen", "AC"; default all.

function.name: call_ha_service
function.description: Call a Home Assistant service to control a device or trigger an automation. Use an entity_id from the Home Devices list in the system prompt, from this conversation, or from get_ha_exposed_entities. Never guess or make up entity_id values. Common domain/service combinations: - light        / turn_on (brightness 0-255, color_temp_kelvin), turn_off, toggle - switch       / turn_on, turn_off, toggle - climate      / set_temperature (temperature: float), set_hvac_mode (hvac_mode: str) - lock         / lock, unlock - cover        / open_cover, close_cover, stop_cover, set_cover_position (position: 0-100) - media_player / media_play, media_pause, media_stop, volume_set (volume_level: 0.0-1.0) - vacuum       / start, pause, stop, return_to_base - script       / turn_on - automation   / trigger, turn_on, turn_off - scene        / turn_on

entity_id.description: The target entity ID (from the Home Devices list or get_ha_exposed_entities).

function.name: control_android_tv
function.description: Control the Android / Google TV over ADB: launch an app, tune a channel, play or search YouTube / Netflix, press a remote key, or run an ADB shell command and get its output. Turns the TV on first. For volume, play and pause use call_ha_service (media_player).

action.description: launch_app (app_id), watch_channel (channel; needs the user's tv_channel_command setting), play_youtube (video_id or query), play_netflix (title_id or query), send_key (command), run_command (command).

entity_id.description: The TV's media_player entity; default the user's TV (tv_entity setting).

query.description: What to search for on YouTube or Netflix.

title_id.description: Netflix title id (numeric) or its URL.

command.description: A key for send_key ('HOME', 'BACK', 'UP', 'ENTER', 'VOLUME_UP'), or an ADB shell command for run_command ('dumpsys battery').

function.name: find_last_chats
function.description: Find the most recent WhatsApp chats (conversation history overview).

limit.description: The maximum number of chats to return (default 10, at most 50).

function.name: search_whatsapp_contact_or_chat
function.description: Search for a WhatsApp contact or group chat by name to find their chat ID.

query.description: The contact name or chat group title to search for (e.g. 'John', 'Family').

function.name: read_chat_messages
function.description: Read recent messages from a specific WhatsApp chat by contact/group name or chat ID. The chat_id can be a chat ID (with @c.us/@g.us suffix) or contact/group name (e.g. 'John', 'ענבל'). It supports bilingual matching (Hebrew <-> English translations/transliterations, e.g. 'ענבל' matches 'Inbal Cohen'), nicknames, and partial searches. When a name matches multiple contacts, the tool automatically prefers the most recently active one. If the name query is still ambiguous after recency filtering, it returns all candidates so you can ask the user to clarify. Voice messages are transcribed; photos and other files (PDFs, documents, videos) are listed by name and type: read_whatsapp_file reads one. Each message ends with its id (`id: ...`): pass it to read_whatsapp_file, forward_whatsapp_message, or to reply / edit / delete.

chat_id.description: The WhatsApp chat ID (with @c.us/@g.us suffix), contact name, or group name.

limit.description: The maximum number of messages to retrieve (default 10, at most 100).

function.name: send_whatsapp_message
function.description: Send a WhatsApp text message to a chat by contact/group name or chat ID. To pass along something someone else sent (a file, photo, voice note or their message), use forward_whatsapp_message instead of describing it in text. IMPORTANT: The 'text' parameter must contain the user's exact original phrasing. Do not rephrase, formalize, translate, or add greetings/closings — send exactly what the user wrote unless they explicitly ask you to rewrite it. The chat_id can be: - An existing contact/group name from your WhatsApp (e.g. 'John', 'ענבל', 'Family') — auto-resolved. - A properly formatted chat ID (e.g. '15550100301@c.us') — use this for new/newly-validated numbers. WhatsApp chat IDs ALWAYS include a suffix: '@c.us' for individuals, '@g.us' for groups. Bare phone numbers like '0500000302' are NOT valid chat IDs. If you only have a bare phone number (not in your contacts/chats yet): 1. First call check_whatsapp_number(phone) to validate it and get the chat ID. 2. Then pass the returned chat ID (e.g. '15550100302@c.us') here. The tool supports bilingual matching (Hebrew <-> English translations/transliterations, e.g. 'ענבל' matches 'Inbal Cohen'), nicknames, and partial searches. When a name matches multiple contacts, the tool automatically prefers the most recently active one. If the name query is still ambiguous after recency filtering, it returns all candidates so you can ask the user to clarify.

chat_id.description: The WhatsApp chat ID (with @c.us/@g.us suffix), contact name, or group name.

text.description: The text message content to send.

reply_to.description: Optional id of the message to reply to, as shown (`id: ...`) by read_chat_messages / get_latest_messages (e.g. 'false_11111111111@c.us_AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA').

function.name: check_whatsapp_number
function.description: Check if a phone number is registered on WhatsApp and get its chat ID. Use this FIRST when you need to send a message to a bare phone number (not yet in your chats/contacts). The returned chat ID (in the format 'XXXXXXXXX@c.us') can then be passed directly to send_whatsapp_message.

phone.description: The phone number to check (e.g. '+15550100301' or '15550100301').

function.name: send_whatsapp_file
function.description: Send a file (image, document, audio, video) at a public URL to a WhatsApp chat. Only for a file at a public http(s) URL. A file someone sent on WhatsApp has no public URL: pass it along with forward_whatsapp_message (the `id: ...` read_chat_messages shows). The chat_id can be: - An existing contact/group name from your WhatsApp — auto-resolved. - A properly formatted chat ID (e.g. '15550100301@c.us') — use for new/newly-validated numbers. WhatsApp chat IDs ALWAYS include a suffix: '@c.us' for individuals, '@g.us' for groups. Bare phone numbers are NOT valid chat IDs.

chat_id.description: The WhatsApp chat ID (with @c.us/@g.us suffix), contact name, or group name.

file_url.description: The public URL of the file to send.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file (e.g. 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf', 'audio/mp3').

filename.description: Optional name for the file as it will appear in the chat.

caption.description: Optional caption/text to send with the file.

function.name: forward_whatsapp_message
function.description: Forward a WhatsApp message to another chat exactly as it is: a file (PDF, document), photo, video, voice note or text that someone sent. Use this whenever the user asks to send / pass along / forward something they received; nothing is downloaded and no URL is needed. First read the source chat (read_chat_messages or get_latest_messages) and take the message's id from its `id: ...`; never make one up. To forward several messages (e.g. a file and the text around it), call this once per message.

chat_id.description: Where to forward it: chat ID (with @c.us/@g.us suffix), contact name, or group name.

message_id.description: The full id of the message to forward, exactly as shown (e.g. 'false_15550101234@c.us_3EB0C0FFEE').

what.description: A few words on what is being forwarded, shown to the user on the approval card (e.g. "Ori's price quote PDF").

function.name: edit_whatsapp_message
function.description: Edit a WhatsApp text message previously sent. IMPORTANT: The 'new_text' parameter must contain the user's exact original phrasing. Do not rephrase, formalize, or translate — send exactly what the user wrote unless they explicitly ask you to rewrite it.

chat_id.description: The WhatsApp chat ID (e.g. '15550100301@c.us') or contact/group name (e.g. 'John', 'ORA').

message_id.description: The id of your own message to edit, as shown (`id: ...`) by read_chat_messages / get_latest_messages (e.g. 'true_15550100301@c.us_3EB01234567890').

new_text.description: The new text content for the message.

function.name: delete_whatsapp_message
function.description: Delete (revoke) a sent message from a WhatsApp chat.

chat_id.description: The WhatsApp chat ID (e.g. '15550100301@c.us') or contact/group name (e.g. 'John', 'ORA').

message_id.description: The id of your own message to delete, as shown (`id: ...`) by read_chat_messages / get_latest_messages (e.g. 'true_15550100301@c.us_3EB01234567890').

function.name: read_whatsapp_file
function.description: Read a file someone sent on WhatsApp: a PDF's or document's text (a quote, a contract), what a photo shows and its text, or a voice note's transcript. Use it whenever the details are in the file rather than the messages. Take the id from read_chat_messages / get_latest_messages.

chat_id.description: The chat the message is in: chat ID (with @c.us/@g.us suffix), contact name, or group name.

message_id.description: The full id of the message carrying the file, exactly as shown (`id: ...`).

function.name: save_whatsapp_file
function.description: Keep a file someone sent on WhatsApp (a price quote PDF, a voice note, a video, a photo) on a saved project item, so it opens from the project; Dana reads its text onto the file (get_knowledge_item shows it). Take the message's id from read_chat_messages / get_latest_messages (`id: ...`); never make one up. Save the item first (save_knowledge_item) to have its ID.

chat_id.description: The chat the message is in: chat ID (with @c.us/@g.us suffix), contact name, or group name.

message_id.description: The full id of the message carrying the file, exactly as shown.

item_id.description: The ID of the project item (entry) to keep the file on.

note.description: Optional few words on what the file is (e.g. "הצעת מחיר", "Voice note about the discount").

function.name: get_latest_messages
function.description: Fetch recent messages from WhatsApp chats with filters for read status and chat type. Media is described like in read_chat_messages (voice transcribed, other files by name and type: read_whatsapp_file reads one), and each message ends with its id (`id: ...`) for read_whatsapp_file, forward_whatsapp_message, replies, edits and deletes.

read_filter.description: Filter by read status. Options: 'unread' (only unread messages/chats), 'read' (only read messages/chats), 'both' (all messages/chats). Default is 'both'.

chat_filter.description: Filter by chat type. Options: 'dm' (direct messages/individual chats), 'groups' (group chats), 'both' (all chats). Default is 'both'.

limit_chats.description: Maximum number of recent chats to check (default 15, at most 30).

messages_per_chat.description: Maximum number of recent messages per chat (default 5, at most 30).

function.name: list_calendars
function.description: List the user's Google Calendars: each one's name and ID, which are searched by default and where new events go. Needed only to pick another calendar; search_calendar already searches the default ones.

function.name: search_calendar
function.description: Find events in the user's calendars (all the calendars they chose to see), soonest first, with each event's ID for update_event / delete_event.

query.description: Optional words to find in the title, description, location or attendees.

start_time.description: From (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, the user's time). Default: today's start; with a query, a year ago.

end_time.description: Until (same forms; a date includes that whole day). Default: 30 days after the start; with a query and no start_time, a year from now.

limit.description: At most this many events (default 20, at most 50).

calendar_id.description: Only this calendar (its name or ID from list_calendars).

function.name: add_event
function.description: Add an event to the user's calendar. Runs at once with Undo; asks first only when it invites people.

start_time.description: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in the user's time (or with an offset); YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day event.

end_time.description: The same form (all day: the last day). Default: an hour after the start (all day: one day).

attendees.description: Optional comma-separated email addresses to invite (Google emails them the invitation).

calendar_id.description: Optional calendar name or ID (default: the calendar new events go to).

function.name: update_event
function.description: Change an event: only the fields given change; a new start_time alone keeps the event's length. Runs at once with Undo; asks first only when it invites people.

start_time.description: A new start (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, or YYYY-MM-DD for all day).

end_time.description: A new end (same form; all day: the last day).

add_attendees.description: Comma-separated email addresses to invite as well (Google emails them).

calendar_id.description: The calendar the event is in (name or ID), when search_calendar showed another one.

function.name: delete_event
function.description: Delete an event from the user's calendar (asks first).

calendar_id.description: The calendar the event is in (name or ID), when search_calendar showed another one.

function.name: run_kubectl
function.description: Read the Kubernetes cluster with a kubectl-style command (read-only: get, describe, logs, top; no writes, no secret values). Examples: "get pods", "get pods -A", "get deploy -l app=dana", "get events", "describe pod NAME", "get pod NAME -o json", "logs POD -c CONTAINER --tail 500", "top pods", "top nodes".

command.description: The kubectl command without "kubectl". Flags: -n, -A, -o json|yaml, -l, -c, --tail (logs: last 200 lines by default).

namespace.description: Namespace when the command has no -n; default the pod's own.

function.name: run_python
function.description: Run Python code on the server (asks the user first) and return what it prints: calculations, data or text processing, format conversion. Prefer a dedicated tool when one fits.

code.description: The Python code; only print() output comes back (no input()).

function.name: create_watch
function.description: Set up a watch from the user's own words: Dana acts when something happens or by a deadline ('make sure the transfer from Maya arrives by tomorrow', 'when the dishwasher finishes ask Gal to empty it', 'remind me at 20:30, 30 min before, or when I get in the car'). A reminder also becomes a task.

request.description: What the user asked, in their own words and language (with the times and names they gave).

function.name: list_watches
function.description: List the user's watches (active and paused; with include_closed also done and expired) with their triggers in words.

include_closed.description: Also list watches that are done or expired.

function.name: update_watch
function.description: Change a watch in plain words ('until Friday instead', 'also when I leave work', 'send it to Gal too').

change.description: What to change, in the user's words.

function.name: pause_watch
function.description: Pause a watch: nothing fires until it is resumed.

function.name: resume_watch
function.description: Resume a paused (or finished) watch.

function.name: delete_watch
function.description: Delete a watch (with Undo).
